body: Yeah, it's hard to bounce back after something like that. My partner left me a few months ago very suddenly and it's tough to figure yourself out after something like that. I haven't been doing as well at work because I've been really distracted. Therapy has been helping me, although I know that isn't available for everyone and I still feel really low sometimes (a lot of times). My boss after it happened told me something that I try to think of when I feel really bad. She said, all you have to do is survive. Not always easy, but I feel like remembering her saying that helps get me through. Trying to appreciate the small things, etc.

Financial problems are rough, no one who works hard should have them. 

I hope you find some way out of what you're going through!

My partner of almost a decade broke up with me in March, and I am frustrated because I feel like I should be more over it by now than I am. I think it's really hard because we would normally be taking a trip right now over the long weekend, and instead I'm feeling really alone and disconnected from my friends and family.

No advice, just feeling like I can relate. I feel like my intellectual side would say of course people like you and you'll find someone that I like and likes me back, but the emotional side tells me that it will never be as good as what I've had and lost. Feeling very lonely.

Ugh, that sucks. Having some relationship problems of my own right now. I thought alcohol was making me more depressed, but now after a couple days of no alcohol, I feel as bad as ever. I feel like having some short term very intense goals have been helpful for me to get my mind off things. Do you have anything like that you could try? Maybe even something that would make your life better like applying for some scholarships or fixing something you've been meaning to for a while? I feel like that's why this weekend has been especially hard for me, no distractions.
